cases.expected: Reject owner/generation mismatch before any read, cache write or partial result publication.

cases.expected: Required checker/bound/builder roots survive through the result; final release drops them without a cycle.

cases.expected: Original source and generation stay owned; same bytes and safe final release.
cases.setup: Serialize a type into a synthetic node retaining an original source node, rotate builder generation, drop direct source/builder handles, then print retained result.

cases.expected: Diagnosable reentry rejection before waiting; no deadlock or partially published result.
cases.setup: Invoke a host callback during a real query or diagnostic serialization, and reenter the same checker from that callback.

cases.expected: Second waits and observes a complete generation; do not misclassify ordinary contention as reentry.
cases.setup: Hold one checker operation, start another on a different thread, finish the first.

cases.expected: Unwind releases scopes; generation is terminally retired; subsequent operations reject; memory survives only while existing roots require it.
cases.setup: Run an actual deep checker/relater path on a 512 KiB worker stack with growth enabled, inject panic after growth, then query the same generation.

cases.expected: No zero/wrap/reuse; failed provisional identity remains burned; exactly-once adoption; exhaustion errors precede publication.
cases.setup: Use a test-only identity allocator near maximum; trigger construction failure, adoption, retirement and final exhaustion.

cases.expected: Rust executes source resolution/serialization limits and diagnostics matching the corresponding native request; stack growth is not a source-language recursion limit. Any unobserved expected result remains pending, never success.
cases.setup: Generate nested object/property and generic relation chains at fixed depths 64,256,1024,4096, with typed queries, diagnostic serialization and TypeToString on a 512 KiB stack.

cases.expected: Native Maybe/False/True distinctions, mode-specific cache results, lazy allocation and immediate-repeat reuse; no universal recursive success.
